subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
subtype: Approach: building a support network early [Action]
passage: On his first evening in the hostel corridor, Dhruv knocked on the two doors next to his and said his name. On Tuesday he joined a study group in the common room, run by Ankita, a second-year who said the maths seminar was less scary in a crowd. He saved the warden's number and his local guardian's number on the first page of his phone and on a card in his wallet. Then he set a reminder: video call with Amma and Papa every Sunday at eight. When homesickness hit on Thursday night, he had somewhere to go. He texted the study group, played cards with the boy next door, and counted three days until Sunday. It wasn't perfect, but it was bearable.

qa.q: On which day and time did Dhruv schedule the calls home?
qa.a: Dhruv set the video call with Amma and Papa for every Sunday at eight.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling on Thursday night, and what helped?
qa.a: Dhruv felt homesick, and texting the study group, playing cards with the boy next door and counting three days until Sunday helped.

qa.q: What could Dhruv add if the homesickness lingers for a couple of months?
qa.a: He could speak with the warden or a counsellor, since these outlets work best alongside trained adults when a low mood does not ease.

qa.q: How might the boy next door see Dhruv's knock?
qa.a: The boy may feel welcomed and glad to have a friendly neighbour, since a hello on the first evening makes the corridor less lonely.

grounding: A newcomer greets hostel neighbours, joins a study group, saves the warden's and a guardian's numbers and schedules calls home so homesickness has outlets.
